about: What named Finnish and EU sources say about saving and investing, and current figures, gathered on 14 Nov 2026 for the coach. Each statement is a paraphrase of the page named in `source`. `checked` says how the figure was obtained: `primary` = read on the provider's or authority's own page or document; `secondary` = from a third party named in the note. Rates change: refresh before relying on them.

facts.text: Takuusäätiö's CEO says credit-card debt should be paid off before starting to save, because its interest is high.
Takuusäätiö warns against reaching first for expensive credit: paying with new loans can deepen a debt spiral.
Marttaliitto says saving in advance is far less risky than borrowing, and a buffer lets you meet surprise costs without a loan.
Takuusäätiö's CEO calls one to two months' pay a good buffer and four months unrealistic for many; Marttaliitto gives the same one to two months' pay as the usual example.

Takuusäätiö's saving tips put the buffer at two to three months of expenses, kept on a separate account; another Takuusäätiö page gives four months as an example and Kuluttajaliitto says a few months of all expenses, so the sources differ.
Takuusäätiö says that once at least the buffer is saved, you can start thinking about investing.
Pörssisäätiö says starting to invest is not hard and needs no large sums; Finanssiala says fund investing can start with ten or twenty euros.
Pörssisäätiö's rule of thumb: the sooner the money is likely to be needed, the larger the share of interest investments; the longer the time, the larger the share of equities.

Pörssisäätiö's interest guide says short-term interest funds suit money invested for under two years, deposits suit a few years at most, and long-term interest funds suit over two years; in its example the current year's money stays on the bank account and the next couple of years' money goes into a short-term interest fund.
Pörssisäätiö says equity investing is wisest for the long term: prices rise over time but can swing strongly in the short run.
Pörssisäätiö notes that a market downturn has usually lasted a couple of years, so plan your investments so that you do not have to sell at the bottom.

A short-term interest fund (a money market fund) invests in interest-bearing paper that matures within about a year; its return follows short market rates, it can be redeemed quickly, and when rates rise its value can dip for a while.
A money market fund is not a guaranteed investment: it has no deposit guarantee and the capital can vary; such funds sit in risk class 1 of 7, the lowest.
Pörssisäätiö calls diversification the only way to lower risk without lowering return: across asset types, sectors, regions and time. A fund is a ready-made diversified portfolio.
Pörssisäätiö says index funds follow a market index, and active funds usually cost more than passive index funds with no guarantee of a better return.
Pörssisäätiö says even small-looking costs eat a surprisingly large part of the return over time; a good rule is to keep yearly costs under one percent.
Finanssivalvonta tells consumers to doubt promises of large, guaranteed or certain returns and not to sign anything they do not understand.
Pörssisäätiö's example: with 50 euros a month at an assumed 8 percent a year, the growth exceeds the monthly payments after 15 years, so it pays to start early even with small sums.
Investing the same sum at regular intervals spreads the purchases over time: you get more units when prices are low and fewer when they are high, so you need not pick the moment.
At S-Pankki monthly saving into a fund starts from 10 euros a month and can be set up, paused or changed in S-mobiili.
Pörssisäätiö says equities have returned best over the last hundred years, about 8 percent a year on average over the long run (it does not say whether before or after inflation).

After inflation, world equities returned about 5.2 percent a year from 1900 to 2020 according to the Credit Suisse yearbook, as reported by Veronmaksajat's Taloustaito, which warns that this is less than the 7 to 9 percent often quoted.
In 2026 capital income is taxed at 30 percent up to 30,000 euros a year and 34 percent on the part above.
A fund's gain is taxed only when you redeem units; while the money stays in the fund, growth is not taxed.

When selling, you may deduct a presumed purchase cost of 20 percent of the sale price (40 percent after ten years of ownership) instead of the real cost if that is better; and gains are tax-free in a year when all your sales together are at most 1,000 euros.
An equity savings account (osakesäästötili) takes deposits up to 100,000 euros; trades and dividends inside it are not taxed, and tax is paid on the return only when money is withdrawn.
The deposit guarantee covers up to 100,000 euros of deposits per depositor per bank.
Shares and fund units are investments, not deposits, so the deposit guarantee does not cover them; a fund's assets are however held by a separate custodian, apart from the fund company's own money.
Finanssivalvonta says crypto prices swing wildly, bitcoin's value is not guaranteed in any way, and no compensation fund protects crypto investments.
Finanssivalvonta notes that the EU's MiCA rules set standards for crypto providers but do not remove the risks: there is no suitability check for the customer and no investor compensation.
The EU's three supervisory authorities warned in October 2025 that crypto-assets can be risky, legal protection may be limited, and promotion by finfluencers on social media is aggressive.

Bitcoin's price has swung about five times as much as global equities (about 54 percent a year against about 10.5), and it has twice fallen by roughly 80 percent from a peak, starting in December 2017 and November 2021.
Selling, swapping or spending crypto is taxed as a capital gain in Finland; crypto lost to theft, fraud or a bankrupt platform gives no deductible loss.

For crypto derivatives such as futures and CFDs, Verohallinto taxes the gains but does not let the losses be deducted, and each trade is assessed on its own: you can owe tax on winning trades in a year you lost money overall.

When ESMA restricted leveraged CFDs for retail clients, national regulators had found that 74 to 89 percent of retail accounts lose money; providers must show their own share of losing accounts, and leverage on crypto CFDs is capped at 2 to 1.
On exchange-traded futures the loss can exceed the money put up as margin, and the customer must pay the shortfall (the US futures regulator's wording).

For those who still want some bitcoin exposure, exchange-traded products that hold bitcoin have been listed on Nasdaq Helsinki since January 2025; with them the loss is limited to the money paid, unlike with futures.

No Finnish authority or investor guide found gives a percentage for how much of one's money may go into speculative holdings; the guidance is to diversify, and to ask whether you would be ready to lose the capital you put in.

products.name: S-Bank savings account (S-Tuottotili)
products.facts: Pays 0.01% a year under 5,000 euros, 0.5% from 5,000 and 1.5% from 20,000. Deposit guarantee up to 100,000 euros. Money in and out at any time.

products.name: Fixed-term deposit (S-Määräaikaistili)
products.facts: From 500 euros for 1 month to 5 years; the money is locked for the term. New fixed-term deposits in Finland paid 2.85% on average in September 2026. Deposit guarantee applies.

products.name: S-Bank short-term interest fund (S-Pankki Lyhyt Korko A)
products.facts: Risk class 1 of 7. Returned 2.1% over the 12 months to 12.11.2026 after charges of about 0.3% a year. No deposit guarantee; the value can dip a little. For money needed within about two years.

products.name: Evli Likviditeetti B (Evli Euro Liquidity B)
products.facts: The same kind of fund from another provider, for comparison: risk class 1 of 7, charges 0.3% a year with no entry or exit fee, recommended holding at least 6 months, returned about 2.2% over the 12 months to 12.11.2026. Not sold in this app.

products.name: S-Bank global index fund
products.facts: A fund that follows shares across the world, for money that can stay five years or more. In this demo it stands for S-Pankki's passive equity funds; the one whose document was read, Passiivinen USA ESG Osake A, has risk class 4 of 7, a recommended holding of 7 years and charges of 0.5% a year plus 0.1% trading and 0.1% entry.

products.name: Low-cost global index funds elsewhere
products.facts: For cost comparison: Nordnet Maailma Indeksi charges about 0.30% a year and a global index ETF about 0.12%. Not sold in this app.

products.name: S-Pankki Varainhoito 50 and Varainhoito 100
products.facts: Ready-made mixes of shares and interest investments: Varainhoito 50 has risk class 3, a recommended holding of 4 years and charges of 1.1% a year; Varainhoito 100 has risk class 4, 6 years and 1.2%.
